scenes.title: The Seizure
scenes.player_knowledge: A rescued POW has given a credible reason that a deliberately taken prisoner could access Gray Fox. Guards must not know that Snake wants capture.
scenes.world_trigger: Guard custody is credibly established by player choices and observable nonlethal encounter.
scenes.state_commit: Capture and confiscation transaction owned by mission logic; retained outfit and equipment snapshot.
scenes.skip: Commit identical captivity state, stored equipment, control rotation and camera handoff; no skipped health damage.

shots.purpose: Establish real guard routes, security truck and one plausible nonlethal approach; no giant quest arrow.
Guards communicate in-world and take positions based on actual detection; Snake does not inexplicably lower a weapon in full view.
Weapon grip released, pouch and radio check, equipment becomes inventory-locked at the same physical beat.
Snake remains clothed and recognisable; cell camera becomes player camera without teleport.

asset_gates: Recognisable 1995 Snake full rig, hands and face
Period guard procedural detention animation
Security truck and authentic custody architecture
Equipment removal props and socket parity
In-world guard voice/radio and cloth/metal Foley
failures: Guards behave as if they know a trap

scenes.title: Gray Fox — Recognition and Intelligence
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake knows Gray Fox is missing, not the true identity of Outer Heaven's commander.
scenes.world_trigger: After player physically breaches the wall and approaches the prisoner.
scenes.state_commit: Fox rescue and mandatory Metal Gear/Madnar intelligence stored when interaction commits, not when actor finishes talking.
scenes.skip: All required intel logged and Fox rescued; retain player's exact unlocked position and inputs; optional replay of dialogue.

shots.purpose: New face emerges from shadow with natural sightline; Fox reacts to the actual noise of the breach.
Snake and Fox recognise one another; leave space for breath and a dry Snake echo question.
Fox's delivery changes the entire mission; show apprehension, not a speculative flash-forward to TX-55.
Physical dialogue aftermath; no automatic guard wave spawned to force pace.

asset_gates: Two recognisable period-appropriate human faces
Gray Fox prisoner clothing distinct from Snake's olive kit
Fatigued animation and lip sync
Cell sound/light layering and Foley
Skippable caption/transcript

scenes.title: Shoot Gunner — Unarmed Confrontation
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake is still disarmed; the recovery route is in the playable arena.
scenes.world_trigger: Player crosses actual encounter threshold after corridor traversal.
scenes.state_commit: Boss encounter begins as player-space fact; attack/health windows never driven by Sequencer completion.
scenes.skip: Boss is in same position/attack state as watching; first attack cannot begin until control is actually returned and telegraph is available.

shots.purpose: Show a practical shotgun soldier guarding an exit and the place to manoeuvre, not a comic-book exposition pose.
Correct weapon stock contact, grip, pump and sound without threatening player during a forced lock.
Recovery-room door is legible but not pointed out by an omniscient HUD.
Aim, footwork and camera match game; boss has a readable first action.

asset_gates: Shoot Gunner identifiable rig and shotgun
Weapon ready/fire/reload montages
Recovery-room door and inventory props
Foley/muzzle flash in correct physical location
failures: Boss starts firing from camera rather than muzzle

scenes.title: Shoot Gunner — Consequences
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake defeated a local security boss through surviving and rearming.
scenes.world_trigger: Boss defeat confirmed by authoritative health transaction.
scenes.state_commit: Boss defeat, Card 3 pickup and slice completion are **separate** actions, not all committed by montage.
scenes.skip: Boss remains down, collectible remains available, no double loot or early completion.

shots.purpose: A clear causal final impact, believable body momentum and actual weapon fall.
Let room noise and Snake's breathing carry the triumph; do not invent grand death speech.
The new access card becomes discoverable and player-driven; no automatic duplicate rewards.

asset_gates: Defeat reaction and collision-safe ragdoll
Retained boss gear/weapon mesh
Card pickup interaction pose
Accurate occlusion and room reverberation
failures: Killed boss stands up after checkpoint

scenes.title: Madnar and Ellen — Earned Technical Truth
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake needs Madnar's own technical instructions after saving Ellen; he does not know the sixteenth charge direction.
scenes.world_trigger: Ellen genuinely rescued and Madnar available in original event sequence.
scenes.state_commit: First fifteen directions captured in replayable intel; the sixteenth remains unknown.
scenes.skip: Log is complete for known instructions even if scene skipped; neither final direction nor a free explosive is granted.

shots.purpose: His daughter's safety changes how he sees Snake without casting 1995 scientist as future villain.
Physical leg weakpoint schematic and audible explanation, not a detached HUD slideshow.
His missing final direction feels human and mechanically significant.

asset_gates: Madnar and Ellen distinct rigged faces
Plausible machine plans and physical props
Lip sync, gesture retarget and writable intel log

scenes.title: TX-55 — The Weight of a Weapon
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake has first fifteen instructions and must infer the final leg placement.
scenes.world_trigger: Player reaches final hangar with required explosives, Madnar intel and a valid world state.
scenes.state_commit: Sixteen validated leg charge placements alone destroy TX-55; cinema only listens for accepted state.
scenes.skip: Laser phase, charge progress, ammo, Snake position, camera and escape state identical whether reveal/catastrophe viewed or skipped.

shots.purpose: Reveal scale first through architecture, then one vast machine; no running Titan boss substitution.
Armour, weak feet, gantry, power and laser cams all read as working physical systems.
Show safe lanes before returning control. Lasers do not inflict damage while control locked.
Charge 16 drives structural failure, alarms and actual object state, not presentation deciding win.
Transition from immense machine to intimate betrayal by the man believed to be Big Boss (production Venom).

asset_gates: Original TX-55 recognisable high/low LOD
Real leg sockets, laser geometry and honest damage layers
Cinematic camera and player camera match
Engineering destruction and audio source coherence
failures: TX-55 walks as default original mechanic
Camera takeover causes unseen laser damage

scenes.title: Outer Heaven — Betrayal of Command
scenes.player_knowledge: Snake believes the adversary is real Big Boss; he has no reason to know the double's true nature.
scenes.world_trigger: TX-55 destroyed; escape/crisis sequence committed by mission logic.
scenes.state_commit: Final opponent is physically distinct actor from the real radio commander; game victory and escape state own mission consequences.
scenes.skip: Identical boss readiness, radio availability and escape countdown; no premature identity unmasking.

shots.purpose: Player recognises Big Boss's public persona; Snake's trust is shattered, not explained away.
Performance holds command-versus-rookie power imbalance, then shifts to equal combat control.
Countdown/AI starts only after a fair player-control handoff.

asset_gates: Distinct hidden Venom rig and convincing public Big Boss portrayal
Credible age/size/physicality and battle animation
Source-aligned dialogue and responsive boss staging
failures: Two Big Bosses mistakenly treated as same physical actor
Cutscene ends with unavoidable lethal hit
